differences.stored:

To remove the radical $\sqrt{b}$ from the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{b}$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{a}-\sqrt{b}}{4\sqrt{b}} &= \frac{\sqrt{a}-\sqrt{b}}{4\sqrt{b}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{b}}{\sqrt{b}} \\ &= \frac{(\sqrt{a}-\sqrt{b})\sqrt{b}}{4(\sqrt{b})^{2}} \\ &= \frac{\sqrt{a}\cdot \sqrt{b}-(\sqrt{b})^{2}}{4(\sqrt{b})^{2}} \\ &= \frac{\sqrt{ab}-b}{4b}\end{aligned}
$$
